“I have a feeling we’re going to end up with a very bipartisan relationship with the Democrats,” Trump [told reporters](https://x.com/Acyn/status/2126088804557836328?s=20) while at Mar-a-Lago.

“It’s a very strong power. You have the power of veto, the power of pardon. They’re very, very strong,” he expressed. “They say in many ways they’re the most powerful thing a president has, and I’m not looking to veto everything for two years, and that’s not what they want either.”
“I have a feeling we’re going to have a great relationship, and a lot of things are going to get done,” he concluded. “Maybe more than would have gotten done the more traditional way. It’s happened before.”
While Trump floated working with Democrats on healthcare, he later [followed up](https://x.com/Acyn/status/2126093046173573365?s=20), saying he was going to “veto, veto, veto until we get legislation that’s going to be great for everybody.”

“Now, I don’t really care what it’s called. I care that the people of this country finally have the unmet promise of guaranteed healthcare in this country,” he stated during his “Meet the Press” interview.

# Abdul El-Sayed catches Trump’s attention with pitch for ‘Trumpcare’
President [Donald Trump](https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/donald-trump) responded on Saturday to Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed’s push for universal healthcare after the progressive Michigan Democrat pitched that it be called “Trumpcare.”
“Donald, this is on the table,” El-Sayed wrote in [a post on X ](https://x.com/AbdulElSayed/status/2120938651358273723?a=Ciynr1ZEO76F68Kcr4c&s=20)last week. “Guarantee healthcare for every American, from cradle to grave.”

However, he said in a phone interview with Fox News earlier in the day that he believes the government could “do tremendous things on healthcare” after Democrats take control of Congress in January.
“They have some good points on healthcare, and they have some bad points, and we have some good things, and probably they would say we have some bad things,” Trump said, referring to congressional Democrats. “But there’s a chance we could get great healthcare and a lot of other things, and we do it in a bipartisan way.”
Trump also told reporters at a press conference Friday that he is “open to great healthcare.”
“There’s a real possibility that we get a lot of great things done, especially on healthcare,” he said. “It can be a combination of what we all want, and we could end up with great healthcare in our country. We could end up better than dealing with the Republicans.”

In a statement Saturday afternoon, El-Sayed said he is “happy to chat” with the president if his intentions to work together on healthcare are genuine.
“If the President is serious about meeting the unmet promise of guaranteed healthcare in this country, I’m ready to work alongside leaders in the Senate like Senators Van Hollen, Sanders, Wyden, and Warren to deliver,” El-Sayed said. “President Trump, give me a call.”

# Abdul El-Sayed catches Trump’s attention with pitch for ‘Trumpcare’
President [Donald Trump](https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/donald-trump) responded on Saturday to Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed’s push for universal healthcare after the progressive Michigan Democrat pitched that it be called “Trumpcare.”
“Donald, this is on the table,” El-Sayed wrote in [a post on X ](https://x.com/AbdulElSayed/status/2120938651358273723?a=Ciynr1ZEO76F68Kcr4c&s=20)last week. “Guarantee healthcare for every American, from cradle to grave.”

Trump also told reporters at a press conference Friday that he is “open to great healthcare.”
“There’s a real possibility that we get a lot of great things done, especially on healthcare,” he said. “It can be a combination of what we all want, and we could end up with great healthcare in our country. We could end up better than dealing with the Republicans.”

In a statement Saturday afternoon, El-Sayed said he is “happy to chat” with the president if his intentions to work together on healthcare are genuine.
“If the President is serious about meeting the unmet promise of guaranteed healthcare in this country, I’m ready to work alongside leaders in the Senate like Senators Van Hollen, Sanders, Wyden, and Warren to deliver,” El-Sayed said. “President Trump, give me a call.”
